Five stars *after* a slight modification. - This product worked perfectly with a few modifications. If you get this part and it doesn't seem to fit and bends slightly outward at the ends, then read on (and be ready to grab a file or hacksaw).

A few other reviewers have mentioned the protruding circular knobs near each end of the part. For our specific Whirlpool refrigerator, there must have been a minor design change since there were no detents for this protrusion to fit into causing the part to bend slightly inward -- enough for the drawer not to fit.

As others have said, once these small plastic knobs were removed (personally, I used a small hacksaw to remove the protruding bit), the part worked exactly as the original part.

Even though my satisfaction with the part rates a 5-star review, I decided to give this 1-star because of the way I typically read ratings. If I see an average rating of 4-5 stars, I might read one or two, but then I focus on the lower-rated reviews to get a better idea of problems with the product that the others may not have seen.

If you're reading this, then, just a heads-up that you may need to slightly modify the part in order to get it to fit -- then it's a 5 of 5.

Defeats the purpose of a Keurig - A Keurig will give you a great cup of coffee, but you don't need a Keurig for that. What makes a Keurig unique is that it brews a cup of coffee faster and easier than any other method -- no carafe to clean, no filters to purchase, and no need to grind beans or measure ground coffee. Just pop in a K-cup and presto! In about two minutes you have coffee. Cleanup is restricted to your cup (and throwing away the used K-cup).

Using a "My K-cup" filter assembly with your own coffee really defeats the purpose of having a Keurig. You have to remove the original assembly (don't lose it!), measure your own coffee (which takes adjustment; you'll probably go through several cups of coffee before you get the measurement to your satisfaction), and clean everything up afterward (it can make a bit of a mess). This is really about as much trouble as just using a conventional little drip coffeemaker. In fact, to me it is MORE trouble, although I think the Keurig uses a bit less coffee and could save some money.

So there you have it. Using a Keurig in the conventional way is the most convenient but also the most expensive way to brew coffee, but using a My K-cup filter saves money at the expense of the convenience.

I was also able to use a power drill, tire inflator, and 600w (on/off) full sized home carpet vacuum for an hour w/ the extra battery during testing. Quick math, divide by 2.

You Tube will walk you through the entire job - My Dryer quit heating... Googled my Dryer model & found a YT video of my exact model that needed a heating element. Wasn't 100% sure if the issue was the heating element or thermostat or ??? I ordered this kit b/c for a few $s I got the extra parts just in case. I replaced the heating element & it took ~1/2 hr start to finish & wasn't hard... I'd say it's 'medium' difficulty depending on your handyman ability. Some will find it very simple to do. My old heating element did indeed have a broken coil, so I felt pretty good about the diagnosis. After installing the new heating element the old dryer is working great again. We've had it fixed for ~a week & done ~10 loads & so far so good. Be sure to wear rubber gloves to keep skin oils off the coils. Be sure to thoroughly clean the inside of the dryer (esp. the tube that holds the heating element). All that dust in all those places is a serious fire hazard. Good luck. I'm thrilled I spent ~$35 & ~1/2 hr & have a good working dryer again... Would give 5 Stars, but longevity is yet to be seen...
